title: Affine basic-open sections of a quasi-coherent module satisfy the two localization conditions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $U$ an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $g\in\Gamma(X,U)$. (1) For every $s\in\Gamma(F,D(g))$ there exist $n\geq0$ and $t\in\Gamma(F,U)$ such that $t|_{D(g)}=(g|_{D(g)})^n s$. (2) If $t\in\Gamma(F,U)$ restricts to zero on $D(g)$, there exists $n\geq0$ with $g^n t=0$.

source.place: exists_map_eq_pow_smul_of_isAffineOpen and exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_isAffineOpen; the affine tilde-Gamma argument of Stacks Schemes 01IA and 01HV

proof.text: Restrict F along the canonical open immersion Spec Gamma(X,U) -> X. Quasi-coherence makes the tilde-Gamma counit an isomorphism, so the restricted module is localizing. Transport the surjectivity and equality axioms for localization at powers of g through restrictAppIso. The first axiom gives a power multiple extending every section; applied to equality with zero, the second gives a power killing a section that restricts to zero. These are the two existing, fully proved upstream declarations.
